blacklistabilityReview.evidence: Falcon's official contract directory identifies the reviewed USDf Ethereum proxy. Its verified USDf implementation exposes an AddressRestrictionSet event, isRestricted(address) view, and setRestriction(address,bool) function; transfer and transferFrom reject restricted accounts. This is a direct holder transfer restriction controlled through the implementation's role system, so USDf has known blacklist/restriction capability even though its reserve dependencies add separate upstream exposure.
blacklistabilityReview.reviewer: SONG Safety Score V9 access review

oracleRisk.summary: Falcon's terms make its internally calculated Spot Price authoritative for USDf minting, collateral-specific innovative-mint liquidation, and maturity settlement. Falcon says it may use market sources it selects and retains sole discretion over price calculation and immediate liquidation; no independent production feed, heartbeat, fallback, or circuit breaker is published.

branchApplicability.rationale: Ruled on an enumerated pricing surface, not on absent branch documentation. Falcon's own contract directory publishes no vault, collateral-pricing, liquidation, or auction contract on any chain: the Ethereum set is the USDf and sUSDf tokens, the Falcon Position NFT that represents an Innovative Mint position, an sUSDf staking-rewards distributor, and USDf/USD and sUSDf/USDf Chainlink feeds that price Falcon's own tokens for third-party integrators rather than feeding Falcon's collateral valuation; BNB Chain and XDC publish only the USDf representation and staking vaults. Every price-sensitive decision therefore runs off-chain through one path. The terms define the Spot Price as "the price of the digital assets determined by Falcon Finance at its sole discretion as reflected in Falcon Finance's internal system, based on data sourced from major exchanges such as ByBit and Binance"; they extend the same sole-discretion determination to Tokenized RWA collateral "using any sources, methods or assumptions it considers appropriate"; and they state one uniform liquidation trigger across collateral types — "If, at any time during the Mint Term, the Spot Price of the collateralised Eligible Altcoin meets or falls below the specified liquidation price, Falcon Finance reserves the right to liquidate the Collateral immediately to cover the minted USDf" — with no per-asset feed, heartbeat, staleness bound, fallback, auction, or backstop published for any collateral. Eligible collateral assets differ only in the strike and liquidation price the user selects for an individual position; that is a position parameter, not a distinct price-sensitive control path. Exactly one such path exists and it is fully described at the top level, where tier privileged-internal-pricing already carries the exposure. The unpublished supported-collateral inventory that held the prior unresolved ruling does not conceal a second pricing or liquidation topology: the sole-discretion internal Spot Price is by construction the single authority for whatever collateral is admitted.

bridgeRouteRisk.summary: Ethereum is the only proven native USDf issuance route and remains in Mint Authority. Chainlink CCIP uses an Ethereum Lock/Release escrow pool plus BSC, Base, and XDC Burn/Mint representations; their local mint/burn roles, pool administration, peer configuration, rate limits, and shared 4-of-6 Safe are Bridge Risk, with normal supply movement dependent on external CCIP validation and conserved lock/burn accounting.

routes.reviewNote: Ethereum is the only proven native USDf issuance deployment. Its CCIP Lock/Release pool is canonical-side escrow and transfer machinery, not an independent native minter; that pool and its owner are reviewed under the structured bridge controls below.

At BSC block 116358048 on 2026-08-16, the verified BurnMintERC20 representation had maxSupply() = 0, the source's unlimited-supply sentinel. Its local MINTER_ROLE and BURNER_ROLE were held by BurnMintTokenPool 0x4b66431f9e5f5cd026ae48e617902207b43048d4; the pool owner and token DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE were the reviewed Safe 0x1e482b60bf19cb1cc859389e0ea3ded153f16bd7. The pool supported only the Ethereum selector and getRemotePools() returned the Ethereum LockRelease pool; current EVM-to-EVM inbound and outbound rate-limit buckets were disabled with zero capacity and rate. controls.label: USDf Ethereum CCIP LockReleaseTokenPool owner Safe

routeChecks.lockboxOrEscrow: At Ethereum block 25770829 on 2026-08-16, LockReleaseTokenPool 0xecf61d6faa3b9fae7195af3bc9891450c1733f78 had typeAndVersion() = LockReleaseTokenPool 1.5.1, getToken() = the native USDf proxy, and owner() = the reviewed 4-of-6 Safe. It escrows canonical USDf for CCIP and is not a native USDf minter.
routeChecks.trustedPeerOrRemote: The Ethereum pool's reviewed remote-pool mapping covers BSC 0x4b66431f9e5f5cd026ae48e617902207b43048d4, Base/XDC 0x33570299e0d73f07c82d005de75de54cf4582fcc, and the separately untracked Solana pool from the current Chainlink directory. The authored EVM routes are restricted to the reviewed EVM mappings.
routeChecks.rateLimits: At the current EVM pool reads, EVM-to-EVM inbound and outbound USDf rate-limit buckets were disabled with zero capacity and rate; getRateLimitAdmin() returned zero on the Ethereum pool. The pool owner remains the route administrator for supported CCIP lane configuration.
routeChecks.pausersAdminsUpgraders: The Safe owns the Ethereum LockRelease pool and its bridge administration, including router, remote-pool, and route configuration. Native USDf mint authority and the Ethereum token ProxyAdmin remain separately recorded in Mint Authority.

controls.evidence: At Ethereum block 25862840 on 2026-08-29, LockReleaseTokenPool 0xecf61d6faa3b9fae7195af3bc9891450c1733f78 remained the canonical CCIP escrow and owner() remained Safe 0x1e482b60bf19cb1cc859389e0ea3ded153f16bd7. Current Safe reads returned threshold 4 with the six owners already recorded, getModulesPaginated(0x1,100) returned an empty module list, and the guard and module-guard storage slots were zero. getToken() remained the native USDf proxy and the pool does not call the token's privileged mint path. Its remote mappings, router, and lane configuration remain bridge-route controls; normal movement still relies on CCIP validation for remote burn/mint accounting.

controls.label: USDf BSC CCIP BurnMintTokenPool

routeChecks.trustedPeerOrRemote: At BSC block 116358048 on 2026-08-16, the pool supported only the Ethereum selector and getRemotePools(Ethereum) returned the Ethereum LockRelease pool 0xecf61d6faa3b9fae7195af3bc9891450c1733f78. The route is subject to CCIP message validation.
routeChecks.rateLimits: At the reviewed BSC pool read, EVM-to-EVM inbound and outbound USDf rate-limit buckets were disabled with zero capacity and rate. The pool owner can change per-lane rate-limit configuration.
routeChecks.caps: The local BurnMintERC20 maxSupply() returned zero, the source's unlimited-supply sentinel. This is a token-level bridge representation property, not an independent native USDf liability cap. Re-read at BSC block 119327110 on 2026-09-01: maxSupply() still returned zero, the token remained non-proxy with an empty EIP-1967 implementation slot, hasRole(MINTER_ROLE, pool) returned true, and the pool's getRateLimitAdmin() returned zero, so no cap bounds pool minting.
routeChecks.pausersAdminsUpgraders: The pool was the sole local MINTER_ROLE and BURNER_ROLE holder. owner() returned Safe 0x1e482b60bf19cb1cc859389e0ea3ded153f16bd7, which also held the token DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE and can replace local role assignments and pool route administration.

controls.capDescription: BSC USDf is an immutable BurnMintERC20 representation with maxSupply() = 0, the source's unlimited-supply sentinel; normal pool minting remains dependent on validated CCIP ingress.
controls.evidence: At BSC block 116358048 on 2026-08-16, this verified direct Chainlink BurnMintTokenPool 1.5.1 was the sole local MINTER_ROLE and BURNER_ROLE holder. getToken() returned BSC USDf, owner() returned the reviewed 4-of-6 USDf Safe, and the pool mapped back to the Ethereum LockRelease pool; the representation's maxSupply() returned zero. controls.label: USDf shared CCIP representation-admin Safe

routeChecks.trustedPeerOrRemote: The shared Safe owns the reviewed Ethereum LockRelease pool and the BSC, Base, and XDC BurnMintTokenPools. Those pools' current remote mappings point back to the Ethereum LockRelease pool; the Safe can change the remote-pool mappings and router configuration.
routeChecks.rateLimits: Current EVM-to-EVM inbound and outbound USDf rate-limit buckets were disabled with zero capacity and rate on the reviewed pools. The pool owner Safe can change per-lane rate-limit configuration; the Ethereum pool reported getRateLimitAdmin() = zero.
routeChecks.caps: BSC, Base, and XDC BurnMintERC20 maxSupply() returned zero, the source's unlimited-supply sentinel. The Safe can administer local roles and pool owners but does not turn those representations into independent native issuance routes. Re-read on 2026-09-01 at BSC block 119327110, Base block 50734519, and XDC block 106715374: every representation still returned maxSupply() zero and remained non-proxy, the Safe still held DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE on each and owner() on each BurnMintTokenPool 1.5.1, and getRateLimitAdmin() returned zero on each pool, leaving the Safe the sole administrator of role grants and per-lane limits under no supply cap.
routeChecks.pausersAdminsUpgraders: The same 4-of-6 Safe held DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE on the BSC, Base, and XDC representation tokens, owned their CCIP pools, and could grant or replace local MINTER_ROLE and BURNER_ROLE assignments. Native Ethereum token upgrade and native minter authority remain separately recorded in Mint Authority.

controls.capDescription: The shared Safe administers representation-token roles and CCIP pool owners across the reviewed EVM routes; these controls can authorize bridge mint/burn machinery but do not define independent native USDf liabilities.
bypassSurfaces: Chainlink CCIP DON/RMN validator configuration and message execution are external failure domains and were not independently enumerated in this review.
controls.evidence: At current EVM heads on 2026-08-29 (Ethereum 25862840, BSC 118819235, Base 50620210, and XDC 106610399), the same Safe address 0x1e482b60bf19cb1cc859389e0ea3ded153f16bd7 still returned the six recorded owners and threshold 4 on every route. getModulesPaginated(0x1,100) returned an empty module list and the guard and module-guard storage slots were zero on all four deployments. The Safe held DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE on each destination BurnMintERC20 and owned the local CCIP BurnMintTokenPools, giving it representation-role, pool-owner, remote-mapping, router, and rate-limit administration. These powers remain Bridge Risk controls; the Ethereum Safe's native issuance powers stay separately recorded in Mint Authority, while Chainlink CCIP DON/RMN validation remains an external failure domain.
